what.heading: What is a variable?
paragraphs: A variable is a name for a value, created with `=`. Every value also has a **type**, and the type decides what you can do with it: numbers add up, but text works differently.

points.title: int and float
points.text: Whole numbers like `14`, and decimals like `2.5`.

points.title: bool
points.text: `True` or `False`, with a capital letter and no quotes.

example.heading: What it looks like
example.code:
vendor = "Cytiva"          # str
page_count = 14            # int
years_old = 2.5            # float
date_found = True          # bool
example.caption: Four variables, four types. Quotes make a `str`, a number without a dot is an `int`, a dot makes a `float`, and `True` or `False` is a `bool`.

demos.label: Check a type
demos.code:
vendor = "Cytiva"
page_count = 14
years_old = 2.5
date_found = True
print(type(vendor))
print(type(page_count))
print(type(years_old))
print(type(date_found))
demos.note: type() tells you what kind of value a variable holds.

demos.label: Numbers vs text
demos.note: With numbers, + adds. With text, + glues the pieces together, so "14" + "1" gives "141".

demos.label: Convert a type
demos.code:
pages_text = "14"
page_count = int(pages_text)
print(page_count + 1)
print("Pages: " + str(page_count))
demos.note: int() turns text into a whole number, and str() turns a number back into text. float() works the same way for decimals.

demos.label: Change a value
demos.code:
date_found = False
print(date_found)
date_found = True
print(date_found)
demos.note: Assigning again replaces the old value. The variable keeps the newest one.

try.prompt: A page header says the SDF has 14 pages, but the number came in as text: `pages_text`. Make three variables: `page_count`, the number 14 as an `int`; `next_page`, which is `page_count + 1`; and `date_found`, the bool `True`.
try.starter:
pages_text = "14"
# 1. page_count: turn pages_text into an int
# 2. next_page: page_count + 1
# 3. date_found: the bool True
try.solution:
pages_text = "14"
page_count = int(pages_text)
next_page = page_count + 1
date_found = True

checks.hint: page_count should be a whole number (an int), but type(page_count) isn't int yet. Use int(pages_text) to turn the text "14" into the number 14.
page_count should stay 14. Put the + 1 only in next_page.
next_page should be 15. Add 1 to page_count (the number), not to pages_text (the text).
date_found should be the bool True: a capital T and no quotes. "True" in quotes is a str, not a bool.

wrong.code:
pages_text = "14"
page_count = pages_text
next_page = 15
date_found = True

pages_text = "14"
page_count = int(pages_text)
page_count = page_count + 1
next_page = page_count
date_found = True

pages_text = "14"
page_count = int(pages_text)
next_page = pages_text + "1"
date_found = True

pages_text = "14"
page_count = int(pages_text)
next_page = page_count + 1
date_found = "True"

pages_text = "14"
page_count = int(pages_text)
next_page = pages_text + 1
date_found = True

pages_text = "14"
page_count = int(pages_text)
next_page = page_count + 1
date_found = true

learn.used_later: Every notebook from Project 3 on keeps page text, page numbers and dates in variables, and a wrong type is a common cause of the TypeError you met in Step 1.
